facts: Upstream officially documents Linux/macOS/Windows, not Android.
The frozen binding.gyp uses the Unix target on non-Windows and links -lutil.
Official Node v22.19.0 android_configure.py supplies OS=android and android_ndk_path, so the common Termux missing-android_ndk_path failure is not assumed to apply to this carrier.
Koffi does not list Android in its official support matrix.
The frozen 3.1.6 is newer than the 3.1.5 release that removed the statx libc-wrapper build problem.
Android/Termux source-build success is useful evidence but is not accepted as APK/NDK carrier evidence.
The frozen lock contains sharp@0.35.4 and exact @img/sharp-wasm32@0.35.4 with sha512 integrity.
The frozen lock also contains @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3 required by sharp-wasm32.
Lock presence does not prove host-specific npm ci materialized optional WASM bytes; the manual G2 device probe checks this explicitly.
Android carrier image processing remains NOT_RUN until a real sharp create→PNG buffer smoke passes.

fallback.loaderBehavior: sharp 0.35.4 falls through to @img/sharp-wasm32/sharp.node when no native runtimePlatform case loads.

facts: @vscode/ripgrep@1.18.0 constructs @vscode/ripgrep-${process.platform}-${arch}; Android therefore asks for an unpublished Android package.
Official DSH tool-fs-search only uses an executable sidecar when 'pkg' in process; the Android Node carrier is not a pkg single-file runtime.
The Microsoft binary line used by wrapper 1.18.0 is ripgrep-prebuilt v15.0.1, built from BurntSushi/ripgrep 15.0.0 plus the pinned Microsoft patch.
Building an Android rg binary alone is insufficient until the wrapper/upstream DSH exposes a legitimate Android resolution seam.
Ordinary LocalSubprocessRuntime.spawn() does not call createProcessInspector(); only spawnTerminal() resolves the terminal inspector.
The shipped Web default preset is standard and does not mount PTY, but the shipped minimal preset remains user-selectable and mounts the persistent PTY stack.
AgentPresets has no preset allowlist; disabling the shipped root would remove standard/ptc/cordis together with minimal.
LocalSubprocessRuntime.terminalInspector exists only as an explicitly documented test hook and is not accepted as a production Android seam.
The official ctx.sandbox abstract provider seam is public and stable in @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox.
Android composition disables only the official sandbox-local row and inserts a Community provider through the official --patch layer; no official bundle is modified.
The Community provider uses official writableRoots(policy), preserves exit-125 plus landlock-run signature classification, and advertises full only after an exact fully-enforced launcher probe.
The frozen runtime lock contains @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run@0.1.1, whose npm payload publishes src/main.c; the Android NDK probe builds that source unmodified.
adb-shell Landlock success is preliminary only; release requires the same enforcement under the APK app UID.
alpha.4 session materialization uses link()+unlink() on every non-win32 platform.
alpha.4 attachment publication also uses link() before removing the staging name.
The gate must run in the APK app-private filesystem; /data/local/tmp or Termux storage is not equivalent evidence.

conclusion: Android Local remains blocked. Sandbox now has a production-shaped official-seam path, but it still needs frozen-source NDK build plus app-UID enforcement evidence; PTY still needs a production Android subprocess provider because minimal remains exposed.

subprocess.reason: Default standard Web does not mount PTY, but shipped minimal remains user-selectable and requires persistent terminal support; AgentPresets exposes no preset allowlist.

officialSourceAudit.note: No alpha.4 Git tag was found. This commit/blob record documents the official source surfaces audited for Android seam behavior; npm package-lock integrity remains the release dependency provenance.
